question_en: In repurchase agreements, repo margin provides a margin of safety to the:
option_a: dealer, if the lender of the cash defaults.
option_b: cash lender, if the collateral’s market value declines.
option_c: security lender, if the collateral’s market value declines.
explanation_en:
The difference between market value of the security used as collateral and the value of the loan
is known as repo margin. Repo margin allows for some worsening in market value and
provides the cash lender a margin of safety if the collateral’s market value declines.

question_en: An analyst observed the profitability and cash flows of firms A and B and collected the results below. Firm A Firm B Earnings before interest and tax 104 million 96.5 million Free cash flow before dividends -12.5 million 8.5 million Free cash flow after dividends N/A - 0.5 million The firm(s) not suitable for deleveraging is (are):
explanation_en:
Both firm A and B have negative free cash flows after dividends. A firm with positive free cash
flow after dividend can use its cash flow to pay down debt or build up cash on the balance
sheet; either outcome is a form of deleveraging and is favorable from credit risk stand point.

question_en: For rating agencies, the primary factor inassigning their ratings is:
option_c: priority of payment in the event of a default
explanation_en:
For the rating agencies likelihood of default is the primary factor in assigning their ratings. The
secondary factors include the priority of payment in the event of default and potential loss
severity in the event of default.

question_en: A high yield bond issuer has offered the ‘change of control put’ to its bondholders. Under this covenant in the event of acquisition, the bondholder has a (n):
option_a: right to put limits on how much secured debt an issuer can have.
option_b: option to change a certain percentage of his bond value with the equity ofthe issuer.
option_c: right to require the issuer to buy back their debt at par or at some premiumto par.
explanation_en:
Under the change of control put, in the event of acquisition, bondholders have the right to
require the issuer to buyback their debt often at par or at some premium to par value.

question_en: To obtain the spot yield curve, a bond analyst would most likely use the most:
option_a: recently issued andactively traded government bonds.
option_b: seasoned and actively traded government bonds.
option_c: recently issued and actively traded corporate bonds.
explanation_en:
To obtain the spot yield curve a bond analyst would prefer to use the most recently issued and
actively traded government bonds. Such bonds will have similar liquidity as well as fewer tax
effects because they will be priced closer to par value.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\7. EXTRA QB-700MCQs\EXTRA 700 MCQs.pdf
question_en: What type of risk most likely affects an investor's ability to buy and sell bonds in the desired amounts and at the desired time?
explanation_en:
The size of the spread between the bid price and the ask price is the primary measure of market
liquidity of the issue. Market liquidity risk is the risk that the investor will have to sell a bond
below its indicated value. The wider the bid–ask spread, the greater the market liquidity risk.

option_a: yield to maturity on a coupon-paying bond maturing at the end of Year 2.
option_b: yield to maturity on a zero-coupon bond maturing at the end of Year 2.
option_c: coupon rate in Year 2 on a coupon-paying bond maturing at the end of Year 4.
explanation_en:
A spot rate is defined as the yield to maturity on a zero-coupon bond maturing at the date of
that cash flow.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\7. EXTRA QB-700MCQs\EXTRA 700 MCQs.pdf
question_en: Consider a five-year option-free bond that is priced at a discount to par value. Assuming the discount rate does not change, one year from now the value of the bond will most likely:
explanation_en:
The bond is priced below its par value but will be worth exactly par value at maturity. Over
time, assuming a stable discount rate, the value of the bond must rise so that it is equal to par at
maturity. That is, the price is "pulled to par."

question_en: The process of securitization is least likely to allow banks to:
option_b: reduce the layers between borrowers and ultimate investors.
explanation_en:
Securitization allows banks to originate (or create) loans and the process results in a reduction in
the layers between borrowers and ultimate investors. The loans are repackaged into more
complex, not simpler, structures.
